title: Enterprise Project at School
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: If the school has a kitchen garden or poultry unit, teach beside it. Keep a simple class record book for any project.

skills.key_step: The child picks a project that fits what the school has (land, water, money, people, buyers) and says it needs a plan.

floor.prerequisite: Has made or seen a kitchen garden.
floor.question: What does a kitchen garden need to grow?

representations: a tick chart of what the school has
the school's own garden or poultry unit
steps: Pick the project whose needs the school has.
Plan who does what and who will buy.
contexts: a tree nursery for the county's tree-planting day
a poultry unit selling eggs to parents
making liquid soap for the school

board.do: Write three projects: fish pond, kitchen garden, liquid soap.

board.say: Our school has no water tap near the field. Can we start a fish pond?

board.do: Wait for no, and the reason.

misconceptions.ask: A school has a dry field and no water tank. Which project suits it best?
misconceptions.repair: List what each project needs and tick what the school has.

listen_for: Start at once with no plan
misconceptions.ask: What should a school do before starting a project?
misconceptions.repair: Plan a class lunch together: who brings what, and what does it cost?

misconceptions.ask: A school has a small piece of land and little money. Which project fits best?
misconceptions.repair: List what each project needs and tick what the school has.

misconceptions.ask: Before starting to grow cabbages to sell, what should the class find out?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to fifty cabbages nobody buys.

checks.question: A school has no water near its land. Which project should it not choose: a fish pond or making liquid soap?
What must the class do before starting a project?

skills.key_step: The child says project money is recorded and belongs to the project, work and decisions are shared, and mistakes are reported.

floor.question: Give one responsibility of a learner on duty.
floor.answer: any duty such as sweeping or watering

representations: a duty rota on the wall
story cards of good and bad project behaviour
steps: Ask whether the action is honest and shared.
Say what should happen instead if it is not.
Say why it keeps the project going.
contexts: selling kitchen garden spinach to the school kitchen
counting eggs from the poultry unit
a group sharing the cost of seeds

board.do: Write: "The treasurer kept 100 shillings from the egg money."

board.say: Was this right? Whose money is it?

board.do: Write "record it and give it to the project".

misconceptions.ask: The class sold vegetables and made 500 shillings. What should the treasurer do?
misconceptions.repair: Role play the treasurer with a record book and a locked box.

listen_for: Hide it so no one is blamed
misconceptions.ask: A group loses some money by mistake. What is right?
misconceptions.repair: Practise saying "we lost it, and here is what we will do".

misconceptions.ask: How should a project team decide?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the team to decide where to keep the tools, then compare it with one person deciding.

misconceptions.ask: The poultry project sold eggs for 600 shillings. Should the class write it down?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the class to remember last month's sales without a book.

checks.question: Who does the money from a school project belong to?
Some seedlings died because a learner forgot to water them. What should the group do?
checks.answer: Report it honestly and plan a better rota
